notes.title: Demo bugfixes update live!
notes.content: [h2]Fixes[/h2][p]Hi all, we recently had new players trying the demo (which is awesome!) and reporting some minor bugs and quality of life issues. These have been addressed, here is a almost complete list of all the changes in the new update.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Fixed clipping with several story meshes[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed collision which could make you stuck in the initial house[/p][/*][*][p]Adjust dialogue and interaction logic to make it feel more responsive[/p][/*][*][p]Speed up the slow walking to make it less annoying but still keep the narrative intention[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed chicken looking like it is flying[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed invisible walls that would allow the player to enter the river[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the nav mesh allowing chickens to wonder into the river[/p][/*][*][p]Adjust font to be more sharper (reduce blurriness)[/p][/*][*][p]Add escape as a universal way to go back in main menus[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where you could see an outline of a character flying[/p][/*][*][p]Make all setting menus rotate so you don't have to go all the way back[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug that would trigger the child dialogue to soon [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Shoutouts[/h2][p]Wanted to give a shoutout to folks that reported the issues and helped made the game better, from the New Game Discord Community[/p][list][*][p]Phantom [/p][/*][*][p]gore_d_lover[/p][/*][*][p]Samuel[/p][/*][*][p]Catatouille[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Blupers[/h2][p]And just for fun, here are some photos of the bugs reported by people[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/8fe19544ea469629aafbea5d9b1842e770913b9f.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/61415b1c46330cebd6f5792cb0408c2222496334.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/b93e294a8665dde724a701d8a57aed638de11fdd.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/92c2fc459a0c56ce6f5c017459c32117cb429c7e.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: GALM - Games Against Living Miserably
notes.content: [h1]Kinsfolk in GALM[/h1][p]From September 8th to 15th, Kinsfolk will be part of GALM - Games Against Living Miserably - which is a gaming festival that is helping to shine a light on how games can lift people up when life gets heavy and raising vital funds to help CALM (Campaign Against Living Miserably) be there for anyone struggling.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/3cf6f406ca1ea488452900be4afae28f0d7b73da.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]What you can do to participate?[/h2][list][*][p]Try the new Kinsfolk demo[/p][/*][*][p]Checkout any of the other[url="https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/curvedigital/sale/GALM25"] GALM festival games[/url][/p][/*][*][p]Checkout the [url="https://www.thecalmzone.net/"]CALM charity website[/url][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Big Demo Update!
notes.content:
Just several months back, Kinsfolk demo went live. And, thanks to you all that played it and submitted feedback I collected a lot of ideas how to improve the game further. 

I incorporated those in the main game already, but also wanted to push a new demo so we can continue building the game together, and as a thank you to the community and everyone that gave feedback. If you get the chance, please give the new demo a go.

So what did change?

[h1]Story and Narration Mechanics[/h1]

One of the main pain points and feedback themes I heard from the players was that gameplay did not feel interactive enough, and that story wasn't engaging.

The main problem was that the dialogue was full of long exposition dumps. To solve for that, I broke it down into multiple segments. Both subtitle- and dialogue-wise. Now instead of listening to the story for 30 seconds, you need to explore and find multiple pieces of dialogues to combine them to understand the wholes tory.


This also allowed me to highlight different parts of environment and reward exploration more.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/5d64c3cd9a54c8a50535162dd0339ac18c61b6be.gif[/img]


I also noticed that besides exploring, there was a lot of feedback about the story missing interactivity. To improve that, now some dialogue is dependent on player actions. Like this small gif, where the story is conditioned on the player's action.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/01ce11c65ab81bf2cbdd0b421b081caaefad6592.gif[/img]



[h1]UI and UX[/h1]

Another big area of feedback was the UI. To get the demo out, I did not think much about the UI, so I did it as fast as possible. But now I made sure the UI matches Kinsfolk's aesthetic and feels cohesive. You all reminded me how much this is important, so I did my best to clean it up. 

Here are a few before and after shots to highlight the difference.

[h3]Controls (old vs new)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/eb11a5ca9e721446fb3383fd2df8cc2a374b8997.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/20120fa66b486dcbcc0681bda5a73ab57d304c2b.png[/img]

[h3]Main Menu  (old vs new)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/ef62425e8c5663ca995ae6c41b394527df89c832.jpg[/img]

[h3]Subtitles  (old vs new)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/271af618e5b239eba9a0526293c18586c3731c1c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/2e3259d5bd76adbb199b3341ffe3349cfdd13878.png[/img]

[h1]Other Improvements[/h1]

A collection of smaller improvements that made it into this update as well. Mostly minor thing related to UX that folks mentioned in the feedback form.

[list]
[*] Better controller support
[*] UI now scales well with ultra-wide monitors
[*] Added tooltips to make it easier to understand controls
[*] Subtitles now are shown one piece at a time to match the dialogue
[*] New animations to make the character feel better
[*] Better movement
[/list]

[h1]Closing Thoughts[/h1]
Once again, thank you to everyone that played the original demo and took the time to give me feedback.

Please Wishlist the game and join the [url=https://discord.gg/HykVF2ecNn]Discord Kinsfolk community[/url] to follow for more.

Cheers,
Vinko

notes.title: June 9th 2024 Devlog #2
notes.content:
Hi all, it has been a while since the last update so just wanted to share some progress and things I have been working on.

I had some personal things happening which made me lose an entire month of progress on Kinsfolk since it was hard to juggle a full-time job alongside all of that. However, I started working again last week and already have some news and things to show!

Let's start :)

[h2]Save/Load systems[/h2]

Kinsfolk is composed of a lot of smaller stories scattered throughout the world. Now that the number of stories grew, I had to implement a way to save progress so when you complete a story and return back you progress is nost lost!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/2fa75729fda337fbb22a5d8820f20a9042805697.gif[/img]


[h2]Working on a free and open-to-all demo![/h2]

I decided to take a slice of Kinsfolk's story and put it as a free demo on Steam! This requires some restructuring since I did not plan to do this initially. I think this is a wonderful way to get some direct feedback from the community, as well as for players to try it out and decide if they like the game (or if they want to participate in building it by providing feedback on the early version).

I am working on this now, stay tuned for the announcement!

[h2]Exploration, discovery and story progress![/h2]

In order to entice exploration in Kinsfolk, now every time you discover and finish a story, you will find out its name, together with a full list of stories that can be found on this level. Here's a bit of that in action:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/432405b884fc522ccebe77655f0863567d18229a.gif[/img]

notes.title: 24th March 2024 Devlog #1
notes.content:
Hi all, thought I could share some things I been working on for the past two weeks :)

I want to do these short devlogs here and there. Let me know if you enjoy reading them and what you would love to see.

After releasing the trailer I got some feedback on the aesthetic of the landscapes and that the animations looked a bit robotic. Below are all the things I worked on and improved.

[h2]Better Fog System [/h2]

The old fog had ta few problems
[list]
[*] it was [b]white which caused it to blend[/b] both with the sky and the snow on the ground
[*] it [b]did not convey well the distance[/b] of environments due to it not being strong enough for far elements
[/list]

These can been seen on the image below. You can see that adding a tint of blue to it (due to the sun being warm lighted) and adding more intensity for farther landscape makes the environment look bigger.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/ae634b9088bf7f7e93307993874467681098031d.png[/img]

In the new fog system below, look especially, at how much[b] easier is to gauge distance[/b] between the two top right mountains. In the new fog system it is much cleaner to see that the one in the background is larger and more distant.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/0f4d64bee5f0cc9aee51ce34ea420595eb166b84.png[/img]

[h2]More Environment Details[/h2]

I got some feedback from the recent announcement trailer that, especially the farm level, the landscape and its details look very minimalistic and plain. Below you can see the difference now that I added more details.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/1f501778b47bc74a8becbd9785a6ea2a02bde07a.gif[/img]

I usually leave these finer details for the end because as I work through the story, I am changing a lot of environment and landscape details. Now that the story has moved farther along I felt comfortable changing this.

[h2]New Locomotion System[/h2]

The[b] old movement system felt robotic[/b] and it was the default engine locomotion system which made it look unnatural. This can probably be best seen in the trailer below

[previewyoutube=Tg83EIEAtMg;full][/previewyoutube]

The new locomotion system added
[list]
[*] dynamic foot placement 
[*] interpolation so animations and actions look smoother
[*] more animations overall including idle animations to make the character feel better
[/list]

You can see this in [b]the foot placement of the character below[/b], how it matches the surface exactly :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44914833/985ca36d0b6526da6dcdecad60694e69dead8977.png[/img]
